findings.defect: _governance_publish_event (the test's publish_event callback injected into the retained create_governance_router) suppressed the SSE publish call when a test-owned _last_replayed flag was set, and synthesized outcome/current_stage/decided_by payload keys that services/control_plane/bff/governance/router.py does not emit. The retained router (bff_approvals_decide, router.py:1060-1061) always computes {"approval_id": clean_id, "decision": decision, "actor_id": actor_id} and calls publish_event unconditionally after every submit_governance_action call, including replays -- there is no seam-level replay dedup for this endpoint today. Reproduction: mounting the same create_governance_router/_submit_action with a passive publish_event recorder shows the router invokes publish_event twice on replay even though the response correctly reports replayed=true, so the prior 'no double publish' assertions passed only because the test-owned callback swallowed the second call, not because retained production behavior prevents it.
findings.fix: Replaced _governance_publish_event with a pure pass-through matching services/control-plane/bff/main.py's retained wiring exactly (lambda event_type, data: _publish_event(buffer, subscribers, event_type, data), no suppression, no reshaping). Removed the now-unused _last_replayed test-owned flag. Corrected the 5 decide-event assertions (approve/reject/request_revision/escalate/freeze) to check the real emitted keys (decision, actor_id) instead of the previously-synthesized outcome/current_stage/decided_by keys, which router.py never sends. The two replay tests (test_bff_approvals_decide_replay_does_not_double_publish, test_bff_approvals_decide_durable_replay_does_not_double_publish) now assert what the retained seam actually guarantees -- durable command-level idempotency (same command_id, replayed=true) -- and pin the current SSE publish count (2, not 1) with an explicit KNOWN DISCREPANCY docstring/assertion message documenting that the pre-extraction bff/main.py implementation (git history commits 632d72a85/106b0ccae, ASK-005 R3/R4) had an explicit _is_approval_replay pre-check that was not carried into governance/router.py during a prior extraction, tracked here as a residual for governed contract revision rather than papered over in a test callback. Production files (governance/router.py, governance/service.py, main.py) were not touched -- out of scope for this test-file-only migration task.
